## 3. Our witnesses

### Patricia Keesey Zschoche (rebuttal): Q2, Q3, Q4, Q7

| What she gives | She inherited with her sisters; she signed the 1992 power and the 2005 revocation; she was never consulted about a sale to Gloria Balane; she approved nothing; she received nothing; she signed neither the 2016 deed, the 2017 confirmation nor the 2017 partition; her 2023 affidavit of loss replaced duplicates never returned, and the same day she swore an adverse claim calling the sale void. |
|---|---|
| Feeds | **Exh. E ¶7, "after prior consultation with us"** (the condition no one else can disprove first-hand). **Art. 1898, "the principal does not ratify"; Art. 1910** (no express or tacit ratification). **Art. 496, "by agreement between the parties."** Const. Art. XII §7, "Save in cases of hereditary succession," for her title as an heir. |
| In her form | Considering that the principal Patricia Keesey Zschoche testified that she was not consulted on the sale to the defendant Gloria H. Balane, did not ratify it, received no part of its price, and was not a party to the Partition-Subdivision Agreement of 15 March 2017, the condition of prior consultation in paragraph 7 of Exh. E was not met, the sale was not ratified (Art. 1898), and the partition was not made by agreement of the co-owners (Art. 496). |
| What keeps it out | Timing: rebuttal answers what their witnesses swear (Rule 30 §5[f]); the late affidavit needs the once-only leave (JA Rule §10[a]) and the videoconference route. Both are with counsel (Note 3). |

### Donata Mabeza King (Exh. L): Q6 through her cases; Q8 and Q9 on direct

| What she gives | Direct: neighbour since 1990; Efren and Gloria's house on the land; Princess and Jomil occupy it. Through her cases (re-direct if cross opens them, or certified records on rebuttal): the prosecutor's 2020 rulings that ownership was undecided; her Verified Answer with the Bicol Post notices, received by the Torralba-Juntilla lawyer on 9 July 2021. |
|---|---|
| Feeds | **Art. 528; PD 1529 §51** (notice before 23 Nov 2021). **Art. 549** (who holds and uses the property). |
| In her form | Considering that the Verified Answer in Civil Case No. 8563, with the published notice of revocation of the agent's power attached, was received by counsel for Jomil Torralba and Nelly Juntilla, the latter the attorney-in-fact of the defendant Gloria H. Balane, on 9 July 2021, before the registration of 23 November 2021, the defendants cannot claim the status of purchasers in good faith up to the registration (Art. 528; PD 1529, Sec. 51). |
| What keeps it out | Not pre-marked and not in her affidavit: it comes in only through a door Atty. Ramos opens, or on rebuttal. Imputation to Gloria [COUNSEL]. Use our Exh. G-1 for the notice text, not her Annex 3-c page. |

### Shirley De Guzman De Leon (Exh. N): Q6, lightly

| What she gives | In 2020 Gloria came to her house, said she had bought the land "mula sa mga may-ari," told her family to leave, offered to pay them to go; later that year people acting for Gloria nailed wood and roofing sheets across her door. |
|---|---|
| Feeds | **Art. 528**: in 2020, before any survey and before any title, Gloria acted as owner of land around her lot and dealt with occupants directly. That is conduct, not notice of the revocation. It adds to the 2020 picture; it does not decide a question by itself. |
| In her form | Considering that in 2020, before the survey of the portion she claims and before any title issued in her name, the defendant Gloria H. Balane asserted ownership against adjoining occupants and sought their removal, the defendants acted on the land as owners while their claim was the subject of a dispute. |
| What keeps it out | Relevance (her lot is next door) and the month of Gloria's visit (Gloria was in Toronto on 28 May 2020). Keep her to her own eyes; withdraw Q16. |

### Francia Abad de los Reyes (Exh. M): Q3 and Q8, only if called

| What she gives | Born in San Roque in 1979 and lived there since; Efren and Gloria "dati rati na nagtutuyo ng mga isda" on the land. |
|---|---|
| Feeds | **Art. 1898** (use of the land, not a purchase from Llamanzares); **Art. 1678** (anything built while they were users or renters). |
| In her form | Considering that the spouses Balane were seen using the land for drying fish, consistent with their own averment that they occupied it as renters (Answer, ¶40), ... |
| What keeps it out | Her Q2 to Q3, Q7 second sentence and Q9 must be withdrawn. What remains adds little that their Answer does not already admit. Calling her is optional; decide by 20 November. |

### Jonathan Paul Zschoche (Exh. K; testified 14 October): Q1, Q9

| What he gave | Identification of the exhibits; his authority under his mother's power; the demand of 18 August 2025 (Exh. J). On cross: no personal knowledge of events before 2025. |
|---|---|
| Feeds | **Art. 549**: the demand fixes, at the latest, the date from which fruits are owed. Authority to sue on the face of the record. |
| In her form | Considering that the plaintiff, through her attorney-in-fact, made written demand on 18 August 2025 to return the property and vacate (Exh. J), which the Answer admits was sent (¶28), the defendants shall account for the fruits received at least from the receipt of that demand (Art. 549). |
| What keeps it out | Nothing further. If recalled, he adds nothing; the documents speak. |
